messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: SRE oncall (eu-central-1) - high error rate and increased tail latency for inference endpoints. Trigger: 5xx rate > 8% across model-serving fleet in eu-central-1 for 5m. Paging Priya and Dave. Please ack and start triage. Logs & dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/inference/eu-central-1/error-rate

Priya: Acked. I'm looking at the regional dashboard. Seeing a sharp increase in 502/504 and TCP retransmits around 03:42 UTC. CPU looks normal, but network RX/TX errors spiking on several G5 instances.

Dave: I see the same on the NLB side — connections piling up. Route53 health checks still show healthy for NLB but the ALB target groups are failing health on a subset of hosts.

Priya: Hypothesis: AZ (eu-central-1a) network degradation and partial instance-level connectivity loss causing uneven capacity and route convergence. Is there any AWS event?

infra-bot: AWS Health: no broad AZ outage reported for eu-central-1a. Recent change: EC2 capacity warnings in eu-central-1a for g5 types in the last 2 hours (internal alert).

Matt: I'm starting a cross-zone traffic redistribution: increasing weights for eu-central-1b/c pools and enabling cross-zone load balancing on NLB where possible. Will also lower DNS TTL for inference.redwood.ai to 30s to speed failover.

Julia: Can you confirm the model-serving autoscaler isn't stuck in that AZ? I see some hosts in eu-central-1a are unhealthy but autoscaler still thinks they're active.

Priya: Autoscaler shows a few stuck instances in draining where the agent couldn't connect. I'll force drain those and spin up replacement nodes in 1b/1c.

Anya (Support): Support is seeing ~12 customer-reported incidents in the last 10 minutes—mostly high latency and timeouts, a couple of 502s for paid Dedicated customers. We should prepare an initial customer impact note.

Dave: Rolling an immediate routing mitigation: add a route policy to prefer eu-central-1b/c for new sessions and set fallback to eu-west-1 for the most latency-tolerant non-production traffic. Executing now.

Priya: I'm SSHing into a problematic host to collect kernel logs and dmesg. Snippet:
```
Mar 15 03:38:12 kernel: igb 0000:3b:00.0: link down
Mar 15 03:38:13 kernel: igb 0000:3b:00.0: link up
Mar 15 03:38:14 kernel: igb 0000:3b:00.0: link down
Mar 15 03:39:01 kernel: vfio-pci 0000:3c:00.0: reset failed
```
Looks like flaky NIC flaps and VFIO issues.

kmiller: These look like host-level network hardware flaps. If dv-switch or host NIC is oscillating, connection tracking to NLBs will break and cause the TCP retransmits.

Priya: For immediate mitigation: 1) drain affected hosts, 2) bounce the node's network agent to clear VFIO bindings, 3) pprof collect for 2 affected model servers to validate no connection leak. I'm scripting step 2 now.

Matt: DNS changes applied: lowered TTL to 30s for inference.redwood.ai and alias records. Also adjusted Route53 routing policy to prefer healthy endpoints in 1b/1c. Note: due to route convergence some clients with long DNS caching may still hit 1a for a bit.

Anya (Support): Noted. I'm drafting a customer message: initial note that we are investigating degraded inference in eu-central-1, mitigation in progress, recommend retry/backoff. I'll flag Dedicated customers separately.

Dave: I'm also enabling fallback model-variants in our routing rules for requests hitting overloaded paths — they can route to quantized variants in other AZs to reduce per-token CPU. Config change:
```
route.policy("inference") {
  if region == "eu-central-1" and latency > 1.2s -> prefer variant: gptq-4bit
}
```
Applying canary to 10% traffic now.

infra-bot: Canary change applied to 10% of traffic (policy-id r-42). Observability: slight drop in tail latency for the canary group.

Priya: Drains in progress. Replaced 6 hosts in 1b/1c and scaled up pooled capacity by 20% in those AZs. Remaining 1a hosts are still flapping — I'll keep them cordoned.

Julia: Agree we should cordon 1a until AWS gives hardware-level follow-up or we evict all affected instances. Also filing a support case with AWS (case #12345678) with kernel logs attached.

Matt: We've seen Route53 switch start to converge ~4 minutes after TTL change for queries from EU edge locations. Some European CDNs are still resolving the old IPs, so NLB-level connection drops persist for a subset of customers.

Anya (Support): Customer impact summary (prelim): ~0.6% of total requests hit elevated error rates; several higher-tier customers with pinned Dedicated capacity in eu-central-1a experienced >20% error spikes. We're preparing individual outreach for those tenants.

Dave: For longer-term: consider adding health-driven DNS weights + active probing from multiple edges to speed failover. Also discuss moving critical Dedicated capacity to multi-AZ placements where possible.

Priya: Oncall handoff plan: I'll keep the thread and run the mitigation for next 25 minutes, then hand off to Dave for monitoring and follow-ups. If anything spikes again I'll escalate to war room.

kmiller: AWS support replied: "We see elevated network error rates on hosts in eu-central-1a; escalated to network engineering. No scheduled maintenance. We're recommending instance replacement and host remediation."

Matt: Good — continue to cordon and replace instances. Also looking at NLB connection timeouts: increasing idle timeout from 350s to 60s temporarily to avoid stale half-open sockets causing backend saturation.

infra-bot: Change event: NLB idle timeout set to 60s (change-id ch-98765).

Anya (Support): Sending initial customer bulletin now. Will update with mitigation steps and ETA ~30-45m.

Priya: Handing off to Dave at 04:05 UTC. Remaining items: verify AWS host remediation, keep 1a cordoned, monitor customer complaints, update postmortem owner. I'll add postmortem doc skeleton in #postmortems.

Dave: Taking over. I'll watch the metrics and coordinate with Support for follow-ups. Assigning postmortem to Priya and kmiller.

oncall-bot: Incident state: MITIGATED -> partial recovery observed; region still under monitoring. Incident severity: SEV2.

Anya (Support): Follow-up: customers notified; 3 tier-1 customers asked for immediate 1:1 status — scheduling calls.

Priya: Thanks all. Next steps: collect logs, confirm AWS remediation, draft timeline of events. Will attach relevant Grafana panels and kernel logs to the postmortem.

kmiller: Also adding a runbook note: if single-AZ NIC flaps observed, immediate cordon + additional cross-AZ capacity + TTL lower + route preferences.

Dave: Closing thread for active mitigation; will re-open if errors reappear. Postmortem to follow. :white_check_mark:
